content.main:
Third Committee 
 
 Federal Republic of Germany  
Protecting Children Displaced by Violence 
“Each year millions flee their homes, willingly or under duress due to armed conflict, 
widespread violent situations, persecutions, violence of human rights and natural catastrophes. 
Nearly half of them are children,” according to Humanium, a child rights website. Children are 
missing their basic human rights. when they are getting forced out of their homes. They don't get 
to go outside and play with their friends and learn skills they're going to need when they get 
older Some kids don't get to go to school and learn so they can realize their dreams when they 
grow up. Countries that were taking refugees have closed their doors. They have run out of space 
and now there is nowhere for the refugees to go. Some countries such as Germany opened their 
doors. “According to recent data published by the United Nations High Commissioner for 
Refugees (UNHCR), Germany is home to the most refugees by far in Europe - 1.4 million in 
total”, according to Statista. But 26 million refugees are still out there and their homes are still at 
war.  
Children displaced by violence don't get a lot of things when they don’t get help but the 
NGOs do help them. That is why the NGO has helped them by giving them clothes and shelter. 
They have provided food too. They are helping them and providing clothes to other 
organizations that are helping with refugees. “UNHCR, and hundreds of non government 
organizations (NGO), called on global leaders to ensure that refugees are included in social 
safety nets and support services for COVID-19 and stressed the need for stronger integration of 
refugees and refugee-led organizations, their skills, and knowledge, in humanitarian responses.” 
Refugees can’t handle COVID-19 that is why the NGO and the UNHCR teamed up and are 
giving them support services. Now the refugees don’t have to worry about COVID-19 but some 
still have to because they can’t get help. The NGO can’t help everyone so that is why they 
teamed up with UNHCR.
 
Germany is home to 1.4 million refugees. “In 2015 and 2016, millions of refugees from 
Africa, the Middle East, and Central Asia poured into E​urope​, stoking xenophobic fears in many 
countries, and even provoking some countries to try to close their borders.​1​ Meanwhile 
Germany—an economic powerhouse with a falling birth rate and a historic image to 
shed—threw open its doors to Syrians fleeing a brutal civil war that had left them unable to go to 
school, work, or lead any kind of normal life”, according to The Century Foundation (TCF). 
Germany is home to the most refugees in the world, mostly from Africa. When Africa was at war 
and Syrians had nowhere to go Germany let them come to their home. Before that, they went to 
Europe but they closed their borders but they soon went to Germany where they let them stay. 
Germany is now home to the most refugees in the world but there are still refugees in the world 
that we are trying to help.
